label: Mathematical coupling (H contains/reconstructs S)
mechanism: If H is operationalized as a time series of built-up area/population/volume ending at the present epoch, its terminal value IS (or is arithmetically derivable from) S by construction, producing deterministic/near-deterministic coupling rather than an empirical relationship. REAL-WORLD CONFIRMATION (execution 1005-3 dataset audit): the official GHSL built-stock-age product (GHS-AGE R2025A) is explicitly defined as 'the epoch in which 50% of the built-up surface OF 2020 was first exceeded' per grid cell - i.e., JRC's own official age-of-built-stock product is computed relative to the 2020 (present) endpoint by construction, not independently of it. This is not a hypothetical risk; it is confirmed in the candidate official product for the single most information-rich H_when candidate (history-variable item 4).
severity: HIGH (becomes CRITICAL if H is allowed to include the present/reference epoch)
detectability: High: inspect variable definitions for time-point overlap; regress S on H components and check for near-perfect R-squared.
test: Exclude the terminal/reference epoch from H by design; use only pre-present growth-rate, shape, or timing features as H; verify S cannot be reconstructed from H via regression with near-1.0 R-squared. Specifically: do NOT use GHS-AGE directly as H_when; instead construct an analogous age/timing feature from the raw GHS-BUILT-S multi-epoch stack using only epochs strictly before the reference/present epoch.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable if H is redefined to exclude present-level information; fatal only if left as-is.

label: Outcome leakage (H derived from R or a close proxy)
mechanism: If a quantity such as 'built-up area inside flood hazard zones' is used both to construct H_where and as the hydrological response/exposure R, H and R share the same underlying measurement by construction, not by empirical association.
severity: CRITICAL for the flood hazard-zone-overlap formulation exactly as described in the candidate design; LOW-MEDIUM for thermal R, where sensor-measured LST and built-up history come from independent measurement processes.
detectability: Moderate: requires a variable-provenance audit tracing each H and R feature back to its raw source data and flagging shared sources.
test: Maintain an explicit variable-provenance ledger; for the hydrological test, require R to be a genuinely independent realized/measured quantity (e.g., observed inundation frequency) rather than a static hazard-zone overlap recomputed from the same built-up layer used to define H.
fatal_or_manageable: Fatal as currently stated for the flood exposure formulation; manageable only if hydrological R is redefined to an independently measured quantity.

label: Temporal leakage (future information used to define historical predictors)
mechanism: If the window used to summarize H extends to or past the time R is measured (e.g., an 'age structure as of 2020' H feature computed using the full record through 2020, measured contemporaneously with R), H is not strictly prior to R despite being labeled 'historical.'
detectability: Moderate: requires explicit timeline bookkeeping comparing H's end time to R's measurement time.
test: Enforce t(H_end) < t(R_start) by design with an explicit buffer; run sensitivity analysis varying the gap between H's end and R's measurement.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable via strict temporal ordering in the design; a design discipline issue, not a fundamental barrier.

label: Boundary leakage (2020 boundary used to summarize 1975 history)
mechanism: Using a fixed present-day urban-centre polygon to spatially aggregate historical values retroactively includes land not urban/relevant at the historical time and excludes land that may have been relevant then but outside the present boundary, silently encoding present-day extent into the 'historical' measure.
detectability: Moderate-high: detectable by comparing fixed-present-boundary extraction against time-varying or history-start-fixed boundary extraction for the same cities.
test: Compare results under (a) fixed present (e.g. 2020) boundary, (b) dynamic/time-varying boundary, (c) boundary fixed at the start of the history window; report sensitivity of H and downstream relationships to boundary choice.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable with disclosed sensitivity analysis; serious only if conclusions are not robust across boundary definitions.

label: Spatial autocorrelation inflating apparent cross-validation performance
mechanism: Cities within the same country/region share correlated climate, data-processing pipelines, and possibly correlated history, so naive random k-fold cross-validation can leak information between train and test sets.
severity: HIGH for Test A/C (predictive-performance claims); MEDIUM for Test B (twin-based, but model-fitting steps still need independence safeguards).
detectability: High: well documented in spatial statistics; detectable by comparing random-CV performance against spatially blocked CV performance.
test: Report leave-continent-out / leave-climate-zone-out / spatially blocked CV as the primary metric; report random CV only as a labeled optimistic upper bound for comparison.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable via standard spatial cross-validation practice; a design-discipline issue.

label: Climate confounding (history proxies climate zone/latitude)
mechanism: Cities that urbanized in a given historical period may be geographically clustered (e.g., concentrated in certain latitudes/climates due to known global industrialization/urbanization patterns), making H a near-deterministic function of C rather than independent information.
detectability: High: directly testable via H-on-C regression/ANOVA, reporting variance of H explained by C alone.
test: Report variance of H explained by C alone before testing H's marginal contribution to R; require within-climate-zone matched/stratified analysis as the primary identification strategy (this is the rationale for conditioning on C and for Test B's 'present-day urban twins' design).
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable by design (conditioning/matching on C) but must be explicitly checked and reported, not assumed away.

label: Development-level confounding (history proxies income/development stage)
mechanism: Historical urbanization pathway correlates strongly with national/regional economic development trajectory, which independently affects infrastructure, vegetation cover, cooling technology adoption, and flood defense investment through channels not captured by the currently audited S or C variable lists.
detectability: Moderate: requires an economic/development covariate (e.g., a night-light-derived wealth proxy, GDP per capita, HDI) not currently in the candidate S/C lists.
test: Add development-stage covariates as an additional control arm in sensitivity analysis; check whether any apparent H effect survives after adding them.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable if development-stage covariates are added to the design; currently an identified gap in the audited candidate design (PENDING_SCIENTIFIC_DECISION: should C be expanded to include a socioeconomic development proxy).

label: Urban-size confounding (city age proxies city size)
mechanism: If older and younger cities systematically differ in size, an apparent 'history effect' could be a relabeled size effect, especially if S's size variable does not fully capture the relevant morphology.
detectability: High: directly testable via H-on-S_size correlation and variance-inflation-factor diagnostics.
test: Ensure S includes multiple size/morphology dimensions (area, population, density, volume) so any residual H effect is genuinely incremental; report H-S collinearity diagnostics (VIF).
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable via a sufficiently rich S and explicit collinearity diagnostics.

label: Sensor/product artifacts (old/dense cores retrieve differently)
mechanism: Thermal remote-sensing retrievals can carry systematic biases from surface heterogeneity, emissivity assumptions, view-angle effects, and atmospheric correction that differ systematically between dense historical cores and sparse new developments, so an apparent history-LST relationship could be partly a sensor/algorithm artifact.
detectability: Moderate: requires cross-sensor/cross-algorithm comparison (e.g., MODIS vs VIIRS vs Landsat-derived LST, or air-temperature-based products where available).
test: Require cross-product replication of any H-R relationship as a mandatory robustness check; test sensitivity to LST algorithm/version.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable via cross-product replication; not fatal per se.

label: Rural-reference contamination in SUHI construction
mechanism: Surface Urban Heat Island intensity is defined relative to a rural reference ring/buffer; if that reference area differs systematically in elevation, land cover, or distance-from-core across cities, apparent SUHI-history relationships could be artifacts of inconsistent reference-area construction rather than a true urban effect.
detectability: High: directly testable by varying the rural-reference definition and recomputing SUHI.
test: Compute SUHI under multiple alternate rural-reference definitions (fixed-distance ring, elevation-matched, land-cover-matched, size-scaled buffer) as a mandatory sensitivity/falsification test.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable with disclosed multi-definition sensitivity analysis; a known, addressable methodological risk documented in the global SUHI literature.

label: Survivor/selection bias in urban-centre databases
mechanism: Urban-centre delineations (e.g., GHS-UCDB) require a minimum population/density/contiguity threshold at the reference epoch to qualify as an 'urban centre' at all, implicitly conditioning the historical sample on having grown into a qualifying centre by present day; settlements that stagnated or shrank below threshold are excluded.
detectability: Moderate: identifiable by reading the urban-centre delineation methodology's inclusion criteria.
test: Explicitly scope conclusions to 'cities that became and remained significant urban centres by the reference year' rather than 'all settlements'; where feasible, test sensitivity to the minimum-size inclusion threshold.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable as an explicitly disclosed scope limitation; bounds generalizability rather than invalidating internal comparisons among included cities.

label: Modifiable areal unit problem (MAUP)
mechanism: Administrative boundaries, urban-centre polygons, fixed-footprint buffers, and regular grid-cell aggregations of the same underlying urban area will produce different numeric summaries, so conclusions sensitive to this choice undermine robustness.
detectability: High: directly testable by recomputing key quantities under two or more alternative analysis-unit definitions.
test: Report core findings under at least two analysis-unit definitions (e.g., urban-centre polygon vs fixed-radius buffer) as a mandatory robustness check.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable via multi-unit sensitivity reporting; a standard, disclosable robustness check.

label: Multicollinearity between S and H (statistical distinguishability)
mechanism: Because H is, by construction, the trajectory that produced S, H and S are mechanically related; the incremental-information test (M1 vs M0) may have very low statistical power if H's novel components are nearly collinear with S's components, making 'no effect' indistinguishable from 'insufficient power to detect a real effect.'
severity: CRITICAL (cannot be fully resolved by audit alone; only bounded conceptually without real data)
detectability: High in principle via VIF/condition-number/partial-R-squared diagnostics, but requires actual data to quantify - this audit can only flag the risk, not measure it.
test: Report collinearity diagnostics (VIF/condition number) for any fitted M1 model as a mandatory output; design H to emphasize components least collinear with S (trajectory shape/timing/directionality rather than cumulative-magnitude features that mechanically overlap S); consider using H residualized against S and C as the operational predictor.
fatal_or_manageable: Potentially fatal in practice if real data show H's informative components are numerically inseparable from S; this is the primary scientific reason a cheap falsification-oriented pilot is necessary before any large-scale investment, and is flagged as the single most dangerous threat to the whole research program (see Q7).

label: Post-treatment control / overcontrol (controlling for S may erase history's own pathway)
mechanism: If history's effect on R operates through present-day morphology (H leads to denser/older building stock, which is part of S's present density/material composition, which affects R), conditioning on S is 'controlling for a mediator,' which can partially or fully remove the true signal of H, biasing the test toward a false null - the mirror-image risk of M.
detectability: Low-moderate via data alone; fundamentally a causal-structure question that empirical data cannot settle without a credible causal model.
test: Pre-specify a candidate causal diagram distinguishing confounders (must control) from mediators (must not naively control, or control via mediation-analysis methods); report leave-one-control-out sensitivity showing which specific S components most change the apparent H effect; frame any M1-vs-M0 result as information beyond a specific operationalization of S, not as history's causal effect.
fatal_or_manageable: Manageable only by narrowing the scientific claim from causal to associative/predictive 'transferability,' consistent with the project's existing governance principle against claiming causality from observational associations (docs/SCIENTIFIC_GOVERNANCE.md) - that principle is scientifically load-bearing here, not merely procedural.
